newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Slight fall in May retail sales trend - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: Slight fall in May retail sales trend - SNZ.

text.p: The underlying trend in retail sales fell by 0.1 percent in May 1997, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday when releasing the Retail Trade Survey.

Actual retail sales fell by 3.2 percent, or NZ$105.6 million, from the May 1996 month to NZ$3.226 billion in May 1997. SNZ said eight of the 15 storetypes recorded falls between May 1996 and May 1997, with the largest in motor vehicle retailing, down 19.7 percent.
Hardware stores were down 12.9 percent, and clothing and softgoods outlets were down 4.8 percent.

Motor vehicle retailing outlets fell by $133.3 million, compared to the $105.6 million annual fall in total retail sales. Total new car registrations, including imports, fell by 10.7 percent in the year to May.

Other storetypes to record significant annual dollar falls in actual retail sales were motor vehicle services, down $17.1 million, appliance retailing outlets, down $9.8 million, and hardware stores, down $9.3 million.
Retail sales excluding automotive storetypes were $2.236 billion in May, a rise of two percent over sales in May 1996.

After adjustment for seasonal effects, retail sales fell 4.6 percent to $3.18 billion from April to May. Excluding both automotive storetypes, seasonally adjusted retail sales were $2.25 billion, a fall of 1.9 percent from April 1997.
SNZ said 11 of the 15 storetypes recorded falls in seasonally adjusted retail sales in May, with the largest in motor vehicle retailing outlets, down 15 percent.
Actual sales in the South Island fell by 3.4 percent, while North Island sales fell 3.1 percent between May 1996 and May 1997.
